title: Vibecoded a TD type game
author: Endlesscrysis
selftext:
I've used fable and pixellab to make a game called keeplings. 

It looks a bit like tower defense at first, but you are not placing towers along a path. You build and upgrade units, place them in lanes, manage workers/economy, and send extra pressure at the other side. Then the wave plays out automatically.

If your lane loses, enemies leak through to the Keep, and your surviving units fall back to help the King defend. So the game becomes less about perfect tower placement and more about army composition, economy timing, and surviving bad waves.

The closest genre is probably “lane defense autobattler.” It is inspired by Legion TD2 and the old warcraft 3 mods, but I’m trying to make it its own thing. 

Give it a try please, literally just got vps/domain and stuff setup so didn't really have any testing yet besides playing locally against AI or against friends with a cloudflare tunnel.

comments.author: Endlesscrysis
comments.body:
Fable did the logic/scripts/whatever. Assetpack used is Tiny Swords but added a couple custom units through pixellab/chatgpt

Flow for the units was:   
Share reference images from Tiny swords with chatgpt to create new unit concept.  
Download the image generated by chatgpt and re-size it to 128x128 and upload this south facing view to pixellab.  
Then use pixellab to create animations, idle, run, attack etc.   
Implement these with fable.

comments.author: alexpopescu801
comments.body: Looks great! Can you explain a bit how did Claude assigned the sprites, was it on its own or did you indicate each of them? Also can you go into more details on how you've used pixellab? Which model, which type of generation, prompt and so on

replies.author: Endlesscrysis
replies.body:
I pointed Fable at the existing Tiny Swords asset structure to inspect it. It saw how the existing spritesheets were sliced/used, then converted the new GIF frames from pixellab into matching sheet rows and hooked them up in the unit config. 

For pixellab I used the custom animation v3 variant.

replies.author: Endlesscrysis
replies.body:
Example prompt for king idle animation.

The king stands firmly in place, his body swaying gently from side to side in a rhythmic, bouncy motion. His knees subtly flex and extend to create a slight bobbing effect, while his cape and the tassels on his armor sway in sync with the movement. He maintains a steady, authoritative posture, with his head remaining level as he shifts his weight, giving him a lively, weighted presence.
